fields.sample_size: 90 household questionnaires (30 in each of three communities in the municipalities of Comitan de Dominguez, La Trinitaria and La Independencia, Chiapas, Mexico) and three focus groups, with water-quality analysis
fields.effect_estimate: Six categories of water-access challenge are identified (sufficient quantity, adequate quality, household and crop irrigation, hygiene and sanitation facilities, among others) and barriers and bridges are classified by socio-ecological interaction; in the absence of formal supply rural communities self-manage water, with community agreements on agriculture, reforestation and irrigation; rainfall uncertainty and women's water-fetching burden are noted barriers. Descriptive classification; no effect sizes.
fields.study_design: mixed-methods multiple-case study (household questionnaires, focus groups, water-quality analysis in three Mexican communities)
fields.section: Full text: Methods (study area, questionnaire to 90 households, focus groups); Results; Conclusions
fields.exact_location: Methods (study area, questionnaire to 90 households, focus groups); Results; Conclusions

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a mixed-methods study of three rural communities in southeastern Mexico (90 household questionnaires, three focus groups), read in full text 2026-10-04. Barriers and bridges to water access are classified under six challenge categories within a socio-ecological framing; community self-management fills the absence of formal supply.
